statement: Fate classes of the Juggler map are backward-closed (J n ∈ A ⟹ n ∈ A): the starts that reach 1 (reachesOne_backwardClosed), the starts that do not (not_reachesOne_backwardClosed), the basin Ancestor · m of any state m (ancestor_backwardClosed), and the divergent starts (escapes_backwardClosed); R and the divergent set are also forward-closed (reachesOne_floorPower, escapes_floorPower). Every start n ≥ 1 reaches 1, or is an ancestor of a state m ≥ 2 on a cycle (Periodic m), or escapes (fate_trichotomy, from cycles_or_escapes), and the fates exclude one another: a start that reaches 1 or enters a cycle has a bounded orbit (reachesOne_bounded, cycle_basin_bounded, reachesOne_not_escapes, cycle_basin_not_escapes), and a start that reaches 1 is not an ancestor of a cycle state m ≥ 2 (reachesOne_not_cycle_basin). Lemma 1.1 of the fate-contagion note. Not a halt theorem.

Certified closure of the Lean seed [1, 260] under the even-block and OE-fiber productions, computed exactly to 10^9 (research.juggler_sequence.fate_contagion, summary.json): every member reaches 1 (Lean even_block_mem, oe_fiber_mem with reachesOne_backwardClosed). Density 0.45–0.49 on every dyadic block (2^k, 2^{k+1}], 16 ≤ k ≤ 29, against 0.25 for the E-only closure; at x = 10^9 the log-mass on (√x, x] is 3.785 (even) + 1.547 (odd), with realised recursion coefficients 0.9998 (E, theory 1) and 0.3332 (OE against the source mass on (x^{3/8}, x^{3/4}]; heuristic 1/3; proved 1/3 on even blocks and 2/9 elsewhere). Classification FATE_CONTAGION_RECURSION_CONSISTENT. A census of the recursion, not a density theorem.

The Juggler conjecture as an almost-all statement (fate-contagion note, Corollary 4.5). Fix N_0 with [1, N_0] ⊆ R (Lean N_0 = 260, reachesOne_of_lt_two_hundred_sixty_one; certified N_0 = 3.5·10^8). The following are equivalent: (1) every n ≥ 1 reaches 1; (2) Σ_{n ≤ x, n ∉ R} 1/n = o((log x)^λ) for some λ < λ** = 0.4926…; (3) the starts n ≤ x whose orbit never enters [1, N_0] have logarithmic count o((log x)^λ) for some λ < λ**. In natural-density terms (3) asks that all but O(x (log x)^{−0.508}) starts below x eventually fall below N_0 — a Tao-type almost-bounded-values statement with a bounded target and a mild logarithmic rate. For Collatz the analogous implication is false, and by exhibit rather than by tree size: {3 * 2^k} is backward-closed under the accelerated map, because a multiple of three has no odd preimage, and its reciprocal sum is 2/3. The Krasikov–Lagarias exponent x^{0.84} is a LOWER bound on preimage counts and establishes no thinness -- an earlier wording of this row said it did, which had the direction backwards; the published manuscript never did. What separates the two maps is worst-case backward log-mass: the Juggler even block carries exactly 1/m for every m with no exceptional residues, while the accelerated Collatz step carries 1/m in the mean but exactly 1/(2m) on every multiple of three, and Theorem 1 quantifies over every backward-closed set. This is a reduction, not a proof of termination, and no almost-all statement of type (3) is proved.

Sweep lemma, monotone pairing, and fiber parity (fate-contagion note, Lemmas 3.1–3.1′, 3.2–3.3). Adversarial sweep: steps in [a, b] with 0 < a ≤ b ≤ 1/2, b ≤ (21/20) a and (H−1) a ≥ 12 give at least H/7 in each half-interval. Monotone pairing: the same hypotheses plus monotone steps give at least H/3 − 2 in each half (1–2 runs when a ≥ 1/4; monotone run-length blocks when a < 1/4). An adversarial 3+1 lock near a = 1/4 sits near 1/4 and is not monotone. Fiber parity: for good m ≥ 10^6 the OE-fiber steps are monotone in [α_m, α_m + 1.02 m^{−1/3}], so G_m ≥ H_m/3 − 2 and H_m − G_m ≥ H_m/3 − 2. Thinness unchanged. Census: mean 0.5000, min on good fibers 0.328 at α_m ≈ 1/3. Not an equidistribution statement. Erratum 2026-09-08: the printed proof of the monotone-pairing lemma (Paper C Lemma 4.1') asserted that every pair of consecutive cells has min ≥ sum/3 because the step scale changes gradually; monotone steps need not change gradually, and the exact witness a = 10/41, b = 21/82, points −2a, −a, 0, a, 2a, 2a+b, … has an interior pair (3, 1). The statement is unchanged and now carries the corrected proof of row J-fate-monotone-pairing-repair (later interior cells are at most one fuller, end cells left unpaired, surplus pays for them). The adversarial sweep (Lemma 4.1) is Lean, row J-fate-sweep-lemma. Lemma 4.2 (fiber parity) is Lean since 2026-09-13, row J-fate-fiber-parity. Lemma 4.3 (thin fibers) is Lean since 2026-09-13, row J-fate-thin-fibers.

Odd generation of two-way closed fate classes (fate-contagion note, Theorem 6.1). Fate classes are forward-closed as well as backward-closed (ForwardClosed; reachesOne_forwardClosed, not_reachesOne_forwardClosed, escapes_forwardClosed; mem_iff_floorPower_mem). For a class A that is closed both ways with 1 ∉ A: every member n ≥ 1 descends by even steps only to an odd member of A (exists_odd_ancestor: ∃ k with floorPower^[k] n odd and in A, all earlier iterates even), that member is ≥ 3 (exists_odd_ancestor_ge_three), the odd members are exactly the odd preimages of A ∩ {⌊m^{3/2}⌋ : m odd} (odd_mem_iff: for odd n, A n ↔ A (Nat.sqrt (n^3))), and A is nonempty iff it contains ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ for some odd m ≥ 3 (nonempty_iff_odd_image_mem). Consequence: every positive integer reaches 1 iff no image ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ of an odd m fails to reach 1; the failure set is the E-forest over the odd preimages of F ∩ S. This is the exact skeleton of the S-fairness reformulation: the one free term of the first-letter decomposition (6.1) is the share of OO-type odd numbers whose image lies in F. Not a halt theorem.

The two exact productions of a backward-closed set A. Even block: if m ∈ A then every even n with m·m ≤ n < (m+1)(m+1) has J n = m (floorPower_even_block) and lies in A (even_block_mem); the block has at least m even elements (even_block_card). OE fiber: Nat.sqrt (Nat.sqrt N) = m ⟺ m^4 ≤ N < (m+1)^4 (sqrt_sqrt_eq_iff, the exact form of the transparent nesting ⌊√⌊n^{3/2}⌋⌋ = ⌊n^{3/4}⌋); hence an odd n with m^4 ≤ n^3 < (m+1)^4 and even ⌊n^{3/2}⌋ = Nat.sqrt (n^3) has J (J n) = m (floorPower_oe_fiber) and lies in A when m does (oe_fiber_mem); the fibers of distinct m are disjoint (oe_fiber_disjoint). Lemmas 2.1–2.2 of the fate-contagion note.

Localized triple parity discrepancy and the OOEEE production (fate-contagion note §7). Proposition 7.1: for every ε > 0, P ≥ P₀(ε), every interval I ⊆ (P, 2P] of length Y ≥ P^{1/2}, and every (a,b,c) ≠ 0, |Σ_{n∈I odd} ψ(n^{3/2})^a ψ(m^{3/2})^b ψ(v^{1/2})^c| ≤ Y P^{−1/24+ε} — Paper B's Theorems 4.4/4.7 with the seven proof steps re-run over I: every displayed bound is either proportional to the number of summands (and becomes ∝ Y) or independent of it and ≤ P^{7/16} (two end cells P^{3/8}, pure passenger P^{7/16}, majorant tails P^{1/4}), absorbed for Y ≥ P^{1/2}. Proposition 7.2: for I(m') = [m'^{32/9}, (m'+1)^{32/9}) (length ≍ P^{23/32}), the odd starts with word OOEEE and J^5(n) = m' number (1/16)·#{odd n ∈ I(m')} + O(|I(m')| m'^{−4/27+ε}) (Proposition 7.1 plus a Vaaler layer for ψ(v^{1/4}) → ψ(n^{9/16}) handled by Kusmin–Landau), and every such n has J^4(n) ∈ E(m'); hence for m' in a backward-closed A they lie in A with log-mass ≥ (1/(9m'))(1 − o(1)). Theorem 7.3: the contagion recursion gains (1/9)·g(9t/32) and Theorem 4.2 holds for every λ < λ*** = 0.5392…, the root of 2^{−λ} + (1/9)(3/8)^λ + (2/9)(3/4)^λ + (1/9)(9/32)^λ = 1. Downstream: Tao rate threshold 0.4608, least C = 18 (fair), C(0.55) = 39. The free term ψ_F of (6.1) is untouched; the gain is quantitative. Paper B §4.5 (Theorems 4.11–4.12, Corollary 4.13; J-parity-triple-discrepancy-localized) now proves the localized and twisted statements in full, so this production rests on a Paper B theorem; Paper B remains a working draft.
